### Yom Kippur
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/yom-kippur-one-year-devotions-for-men-september-28.html
Passage: Leviticus 16:30
Points:
- God chose to dwell in the wilderness tabernacle, but human sinfulness regularly contaminated His dwelling place.
- Annual cleansing rituals were commanded to purify the sacred space, the priests, and the entire assembly.
- The two goats vividly demonstrated divine substitution and the complete removal of sin from sight and memory.
- The Old Testament ceremonial system served its purpose and pointed ahead to the ultimate fulfillment found in Christ.
- Jesus’ sacrificial death secures lasting forgiveness, enabling believers to respond with joyful reverence.

### The Purpose of the Old Testament Scapegoat
Author: Jennifer Waddle
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-bible-verse/the-purpose-of-the-old-testament-scapegoat-bible-study-minute-january-10-2018.html
Passage: Leviticus 16:21-22
Points:
- The high priest laid hands on the live goat to symbolically place Israel’s sins upon its head.
- The scapegoat was sent far into the wilderness so the people's guilt would never return to the community.
- Jesus served as the true sin-bearer by taking our actual guilt and shame upon Himself on the cross.
- Christ’s once-for-all sacrifice ended the need for recurring annual ceremonies to clean our record.
- Believers can rest assured knowing their transgressions have been completely removed as far as the east is from the west.

### Free
Author: Mike DeVries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/homeword-nov-27-2007-11560313.html
Passage: Leviticus 16:20-22
Points:
- The high point of the Day of Atonement involved sending a guilt-laden live goat out into the desert.
- God gave Israel this ritual to illustrate that sin was not merely covered, but entirely removed.
- Releasing the goat prompted joyful celebration because the community knew their sins were gone for good.
- Jesus’ work on the cross accomplished more than temporary appeasement; He carried our guilt away permanently.
- When past failures linger in memory, Christians should stand firm in the freedom of Christ's complete forgiveness.

### Entering the Holy Place
Author: L. Michael Morales
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/entering-holy-place
Passage: Leviticus 16:1–34
Points:
- The Day of Atonement serves as the theological center of Leviticus and the wider Pentateuch.
- Entering God's earthly throne room required an anointed high priest carrying sacrificial blood.
- Old Testament history illustrates that attempting to approach God outside of His designated mediator brings death.
- Jesus is the true High Priest who justifies our approach to God through His death and resurrection.
- Christians can now approach God’s presence in worship with confident assurance, profound awe, and great joy.
